technical.lead: Ollama 0.31 enables multi-token prediction for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon
technical.body: Ollama shipped version 0.31 on July 1, 2026 with multi-token prediction (MTP) on by default for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon, reporting the model now generates tokens nearly 90% faster on average across a coding-agent benchmark with no change to output. The mechanism is in-model speculative decoding: Gemma 4 ships a small draft model that proposes several next tokens and the main model verifies them in one pass, so multiple tokens land for roughly the cost of one when the draft is right. Ollama also contributed a small-batch matmul kernel to Apple's MLX framework that unpacks each weight block once and reuses it across the batch, making Gemma 4's largest matmuls 2x-2.5x faster on an M5 Max with nvfp4, and the kernel is reusable by other MLX models. The 0.30.11-0.31 train also added thinking-capability detection, Claude Code and opencode auto-install hooks, Codex drift detection, and CUDA sm_86 support, per the Ollama release notes. Because coding agents call the model continuously and code is unusually predictable, draft acceptance is high and the speedup compounds over a session, closing part of the gap between on-device agentic throughput and hosted inference without new hardware.

technical.lead: Together AI raises $800M Series C at $8.3B, led by Aramco's Prosperity7
technical.body: Together AI announced an $800 million Series C at an $8.3 billion post-money valuation on July 1, 2026, a 2.5x step-up from its $3.3 billion February 2025 Series B and bringing total funding to $1.3 billion. The round was led by Aramco Ventures' Prosperity7 Ventures US, with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, NVIDIA, March Capital, Pegatron, and SentinelOne's S Ventures participating, per DataCenter Dynamics. What sets it apart from the frontier-lab mega-rounds is where the money sits: Together AI is a neocloud that trains and serves open-weight models such as DeepSeek, Nemotron, MiniMax, and Kimi at a fraction of closed-model cost, and it expects its GPU-infrastructure footprint to grow roughly 50-fold over five years. Prosperity7 managing director Abhishek Shukla framed the company as headed for the public markets. The signal for teams choosing an inference vendor is that the open-model hosting layer is now being capitalized as a durable platform in its own right, alongside peers like Fireworks and Baseten, with the open question being whether owned-GPU open-model inference can keep undercutting hosted frontier APIs on price while matching them on latency.

technical.lead: Tenstorrent's Jim Keller denies Qualcomm buyout talks, cooling an $8-10B deal
technical.body: At a Tokyo media event, Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller said on June 30, 2026 and reiterated into July 3 that the AI-chip startup is not in acquisition discussions with Qualcomm, directly countering a mid-June report, originating with The Information and picked up by Reuters, that Qualcomm was weighing a full buyout at a reported $8 billion to $10 billion, per GuruFocus. Keller said the company is focused on building its own business, including IP licensing and high-end scalable AI work anchored in Japan, while leaving the door open to partnerships. The denial matters because it removes, for now, a consolidation path that would have folded one of the few credible RISC-V-based accelerator IP houses into a mobile-SoC incumbent, and it lands while Tenstorrent is mid-stride on an IPO bridge and confidential S-1 track rather than shopping itself. For buyers evaluating the non-NVIDIA accelerator field, the takeaway is that Tenstorrent's Galaxy rack roadmap and IP-licensing model remain on an independent trajectory. The broader read is that the memory-bandwidth and inference-ASIC race is now valuable enough for acquisition rumors to move markets, yet the leading independents are choosing public offerings over sale.

technical.lead: Stathera closes $55M Series B for MEMS silicon timing in AI data centers
technical.body: Montreal-based Stathera announced an oversubscribed $55 million Series B on June 30, 2026, led by new investor Maverick Silicon with Celesta Capital, BDC Capital, MediaTek Innovation Fund, TXC Corporation, and Ultratech Capital Partners participating, bringing total funding to $75 million, per citybiz. Stathera builds MEMS-based precision timing on a proprietary DualMode architecture that replaces legacy quartz oscillators with semiconductor timing, claiming roughly 85% smaller footprints plus better shock and vibration resilience. The round will ramp mass production of its second-generation 32.768 kHz portfolio, open a Silicon Valley office to court hyperscale customers, and fund a GEN3 platform aimed at communications, enterprise, and AI-data-center clocks, with first customer samples targeted for 2028. The company pegs the AI-data-center time-synchronization opportunity at about $1.5 billion cumulatively through 2030 within an $11 billion annual timing market. The reason a clock startup shows up in an AI briefing is that as accelerator clusters scale to tens of thousands of GPUs, precise resilient timing across nodes becomes a real constraint on interconnect and throughput. With a 2028 sampling horizon this is a directional bet rather than a shipping product, but it marks timing as a named line item in AI-datacenter buildouts.

technical.lead: Geneva AI Week and an AI Tinkerers SF meetup open a stacked fall event slate
technical.body: The nearest catalyst is Geneva AI Week, July 6-10, 2026 at the Palexpo center, opening with the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (July 6-7) and rolling into the ITU AI for Good Summit (July 7-10), where a new UN AI for Good Commission co-chaired by Salesforce's Marc Benioff and Rwanda's Paul Kagame, seating Jensen Huang, Andy Jassy, Brad Smith, and Anthropic's Jack Clark, holds its first meeting July 8. For Bay Area locals, AI Tinkerers San Francisco hosts a GTM-engineering meetup on July 8. On the hardware track, AMD's MI400 Instinct series and "Helios" rack-scale system remain the marquee 2H-2026 catalyst, with the nearest confirmed gathering being Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford on August 23-25 (early registration closes July 31) and the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17. The AI-security block clusters in early-to-mid August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas, and OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6. On the enterprise track, Ai4 2026 runs August 4-6 in Las Vegas, with GitHub Universe on October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent November 30 to December 4. The two immediate actions are the July 6-10 Geneva sessions for governance and the July 8 AI Tinkerers SF meetup for locals; the August AI Risk Summit and Hot Chips are the natural next venues for confidential-inference and secure-accelerator announcements.
